title: Benjamin of Tudela journeyed and recorded the Jewish communities of the world; his book was translated into almost every European language

trailer.text: Benjamin of Tudela was a 12th-century Jewish traveler, known for the detailed account he wrote of his journeys through Europe, the Middle East and North Africa.
Benjamin ben Jonah of Tudela lived in the second half of the 12th century, and according to the Encyclopaedia Judaica he was the greatest Jewish traveler of the Middle Ages.
According to the preface to his book, he set out from Tudela, his city, and passed through many remote countries.
In every place he entered, he recorded what he saw or what trustworthy persons told him.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, he described the Jews in all those lands: their standing, their occupations, their schools and their leading men.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, his book of travels was translated into almost every language of Europe.

stations.title: Before the journey: a world of Crusades

paragraphs.text: According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, Benjamin of Tudela was a celebrated traveler of the 12th century, and beyond his journey no facts of his life are known.
According to the preface to the book of travels, he came from Tudela in Navarre, and his father's name was Jonah.
According to JTA, he was a Spanish Jew, a scholar and a merchant.

According to Adler, during the period of the Crusades the most prosperous communities in Germany and the Jewish communities along the route to the Land of Israel were destroyed or dispersed, and according to JTA, in the First Crusade at the end of the 11th century the Franks massacred the Jews of France and Germany before continuing to the Holy Land.
According to JTA, during the First Crusade, at the end of the 11th century, the Franks massacred the Jews of France and Germany before continuing to the Holy Land.
According to Adler, in the period of the Crusades the most prosperous communities in Germany and the communities along the route to the Land of Israel were exterminated or dispersed.
According to JTA, Benjamin does not say why he set out on his journey.
According to Adler, he may have set out to find where his expatriated brethren could find asylum.
According to EBSCO as well, he may have hoped to find places of asylum for Jews.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, some have suggested that he was a gem merchant.
According to EBSCO, his careful description of commerce indicates that he was probably a merchant by profession.

stations.title: The route: from Spain to Baghdad, and back

paragraphs.text: According to the preface, Benjamin set out from Tudela, his city, and passed through many remote countries.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, on his way east he passed through Catalonia, southern France, Italy, Greece, the islands of the Levant, Syria, the Land of Israel and Mesopotamia, to Baghdad.
On the way back, according to the same source, he passed through Khuzistan, the Indian Ocean and Yemen to Egypt, where he stayed a long time.
From there, by way of Sicily, he returned to Spain.
According to JTA, Benjamin returned home after visiting more than 300 cities and seeing many extraordinary sights.
According to EBSCO, he mentioned nearly three hundred places.
The places given the most coverage are Rome, Constantinople, Nablus, Jerusalem, Damascus, Baghdad, Cairo and Alexandria.
According to JTA, he did this about a century before Marco Polo.

stations.title: How he worked: notes in every city

paragraphs.text: According to the preface, in every place he entered Benjamin recorded all that he saw or what trustworthy persons told him.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the book was compiled from the notes he made on the spot and brought with him to Castile in 1173.
According to the same source, the author of the preface, whose name is unknown, probably compiled the account for Benjamin from the notes.
According to Legado Andalusí, the book's main aim was to report on the social and cultural situation of the Jewish communities throughout the known world.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, Benjamin recorded data on the civil standing of the Jews, their occupations, their schools and their leading men.
According to the same source, his book contains the names of no less than 248 people he knew.

stations.title: What he saw in the West: Rome, Narbonne, Greece and Constantinople

paragraphs.text: According to Benjamin, Narbonne is a city pre-eminent for learning, and from there the Torah goes forth to all countries.
In Rome, according to his description, lived about 200 Jews, who held an honourable position and paid no tax.
Rabbi Jehiel, of the Jews of Rome, was, according to Benjamin, a member of the Pope's court and the steward of his house.
In the Church of St. John in the Lateran he saw, by his account, two bronze columns taken from the Temple.
In Brindisi, according to Benjamin, lived about ten Jews who worked as dyers.
In Crissa lived about 200 Jews, who sowed and reaped on their own land.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the large Jewish community of Thebes in Greece was engaged in the manufacture of silk and purple.
According to EBSCO, in Constantinople Jews were not permitted to be within the city, except one who was the emperor's physician.
According to EBSCO, thanks to the physician the oppression of the Jews who lived outside the city was somewhat alleviated.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, he also mentioned the Jewish tanners there.
According to EBSCO, he estimated that Constantinople received twenty thousand gold pieces a year as tax from merchants and from the rent of shops and markets.

stations.title: What he saw in the East: Baghdad, Cairo, tombs and sects

paragraphs.text: Jerusalem and Damascus were among the places given the most coverage in the book.
In Baghdad, according to Benjamin, the head of the Jews was Daniel son of Hisdai, the Head of the Exile.
According to EBSCO, Benjamin noted that Baghdad had twenty-eight synagogues and ten academies.
According to Legado Andalusí, in Cairo Benjamin counted no less than seven thousand Jews, rich and scholars of the Torah.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, he described the tomb of the prophet Ezekiel and the solemn ceremonies there.
His account of David Alroy, the false messiah, is according to the same source the chief source for that chapter of Jewish history.
According to JTA, in Cyprus Benjamin found a heretical sect that ushered in the Sabbath on Saturday morning.
According to JTA, in certain places, such as Constantinople and Rudbar in Persia, Jews were violently oppressed, but this was the exception to the rule.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, his account of the Druze is the first in non-Arabic literature.
According to EBSCO, he was the first from the West to describe accurately the sect of the Assassins in Syria and Iran, and the first to mention China by its modern name.

stations.title: The book: from Castile to print

paragraphs.text: According to the Hebrew preface, Benjamin brought the book with him on his return to Castile in the year 4933, that is, 1173 CE.
According to Legado Andalusí, he probably travelled between 1165 and 1173 and died around 1175, without having much time to write or to organize his numerous observations.
According to JTA, the book was written in Hebrew with many Arabic grammatical forms.
According to the Hebrew preface, wherever his statements were tested they were found accurate and consistent, for he is a trustworthy man.
According to JTA, it is the most detailed depiction of everyday life in the Middle Ages that has come down to us.
According to EBSCO, it is the fullest and most accurate record of the condition and numbers of the Jews in the 12th century.
According to Adler, the first edition was printed in Constantinople in 1543 by Eliezer ben Gershon.
The first volume of Asher's edition, with a vocalized Hebrew text and an English translation, appeared in 1840.
According to JTA, Renaissance scholars discovered the book, and it was translated into many European languages.
According to JTA, Benjamin inspired major works of literature.
According to JTA, scholars have questioned many aspects of the narrative, and some have charged that Benjamin inflated the numbers of Jews and exaggerated their accomplishments.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, it is not always clear whether he is counting individuals or householders, and in cases such as Baghdad the figures seem exaggerated.
According to JTA, Benjamin did not make clear that his descriptions of China and Tibet were not based on personal experience, since he never reached them.
According to EBSCO, most scholars believe that his accounts of the places beyond the Persian Gulf are based on what he heard from merchants and travelers in Baghdad.
According to EBSCO, regarding what he claimed to have seen himself, very few significant errors have been exposed.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the book is perhaps not altogether free from fiction, but it is marked by sobriety, clarity and a concise style.

disagreements.question: When did Benjamin set out on his journey?

versions.says: Jewish Encyclopedia: he set out from Saragossa in 1160
EBSCO: he left Tudela in 1159 or 1160

disagreements.question: How long did the journey last?

versions.says: Jewish Encyclopedia: thirteen years, from 1160 to 1173
Encyclopaedia Judaica: a minimum of 5 years and a maximum of 14 years

disagreements.question: How many Jews lived in Baghdad?

versions.says: According to EBSCO, Benjamin noted forty thousand Jews
My Jewish Learning: the figure is greatly exaggerated, and scholars estimate there were closer to 4000

disagreements.question: In what year did Benjamin die?

versions.says: EBSCO: in 1173, the year he returned to Spain

disagreements.question: In what year was the Ferrara edition printed?

versions.says: University of Granada database: a manuscript recorded as a copy of the Ferrara 1555 edition
EBSCO: the Hebrew preface describes him as a rabbi, and he demonstrated familiarity with rabbinical literature
Encyclopaedia Judaica: there is no authority for the title Rabbi; it is only a conventional abbreviation preceding his name in the Hebrew sources

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, בנימין בן יונה מטודלה (המחצית השנייה של המאה ה-12) היה הנוסע היהודי הגדול ביותר בימי הביניים.
claims.quote: BENJAMIN (Ben Jonah) OF TUDELA (second half of 12th century), the greatest medieval Jewish traveler.

claims.text: לפי ההקדמה העברית, בנימין יצא מטודלה עירו ועבר בארצות רחוקות רבות, כפי שמסופר בספרו.
claims.quote: set forth from Tudela, his native city, and passed through many remote countries, as is related in his book

claims.text: לפי ההקדמה, בכל מקום שנכנס אליו רשם את כל מה שראה או שסיפרו לו אנשים נאמנים.
claims.quote: In every place which he entered, he made a record of all that he saw, or was told of by trustworthy persons

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, בנימין תיאר את היהודים בכל הארצות האלה, עם נתונים מדויקים על מעמדם האזרחי, עיסוקיהם, בתי הספר והאישים המובילים שלהם.
claims.quote: he gives full descriptions of the Jews living in all those lands, with accurate data about them, their civil standing, their occupations, their schools, and their leading men.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, חשיבות היצירה נמדדת בכך שתורגמה כמעט לכל שפה באירופה.
claims.quote: The importance of the work can be gauged from the fact that it has been translated into almost every language of Europe

claims.text: לפי הקדמת ספר המסעות, בנימין בא מטודלה שבנווארה ושם אביו יונה.
claims.quote: he came from Tudela in Navarre, and that his father's name was Jonah

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, בנימין מטודלה היה נוסע מפורסם של המאה ה-12, ומלבד מסעו לא ידועות עובדות על חייו.
claims.quote: A celebrated traveler of the twelfth century. Beyond his journey, no facts of his life are known.

claims.text: לפי ההקדמה העברית, בנימין הביא את הספר בשובו לקסטיליה בשנת 4933 (1173 לספירה).
claims.quote: He brought this book with him on his return to the country of Castile, in the year 4933 (C.E. 1173)

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, בדרכו מזרחה עבר בנימין בקטלוניה, דרום צרפת, איטליה, יוון, איי הלבנט, סוריה, ארץ ישראל ומסופוטמיה עד בגדאד.
claims.quote: Benjamin's route to the East took him through Catalonia, southern France, Italy, Greece, the islands of the Levant, Syria, Palestine, and Mesopotamia, to Bagdad.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, בדרך חזרה עבר בנימין בחוזיסטן, באוקיינוס ההודי ובתימן למצרים, שם שהה זמן רב, ומשם דרך סיציליה חזר לספרד.
claims.quote: His homeward journey lay through Khuzistan, the Indian ocean, and Yemen, to Egypt, where he stayed a long time; thence by way of Sicily back to Spain.

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, בנימין הזכיר כמעט שלוש מאות מקומות, ואלה שזכו לכיסוי הרב ביותר הם רומא, קושטא, שכם, ירושלים, דמשק, בגדאד, קהיר ואלכסנדריה.
claims.quote: Of the nearly three hundred locations mentioned by Benjamin, those communities given the most coverage are Rome, Constantinople, Nablus, Jerusalem, Damascus, Baghdad, Cairo, and Alexandria.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, ספרו מכיל שמות של לא פחות מ-248 אנשים שהכיר.
claims.quote: His book thus contains the names of no less than 248 of those he knew, among them many well known to history.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, מסעות בנימין מטודלה פורסמו לראשונה בקושטא ב-1543.
claims.quote: The Itinerary of Benjamin of Tudela was first published at Constantinople in 1543

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, מסעו נמשך שלוש עשרה שנים: הוא יצא מסרגוסה ב-1160 וחזר לספרד ב-1173.
claims.quote: His journey occupied thirteen years: setting out from Saragossa in 1160, he was back again in Spain in 1173.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, תחילת מסעותיו מתוארכת לסביבות 1159 או לסביבות 1167, והוא חזר לספרד ב-4933 (1172/73).
claims.quote: From internal evidence the beginning of his journeys has been dated either about 1159 or about 1167, and he returned to Spain in 4933 (1172/73).

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, בנימין עזב את טודלה ב-1159 או ב-1160 וחזר לספרד עד 1173, השנה שבה מת.
claims.quote: He left Tudela in 1159 or 1160 and was back in Spain by 1173, the year in which he died.

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, בנימין יצא ב-1165/6 למסע באזור הים התיכון, מסופוטמיה, ארץ ישראל, ערב, מצרים ואסיה הקטנה והמזרח הקרוב.
claims.quote: In 1165/6, he set off on a voyage through the Mediterranean region, Mesopotamia, Palestine, Arabia, Egypt, and other parts of Asia Minor and the Near East

claims.text: לפי JTA, בנימין מטודלה היה ספרדי בן המאה ה-12, איש רוח וסוחר, שנסע בתפוצות ותיעד את כל מה שראה.
claims.quote: Benjamin of Tudela, the 12th-century Spanish scholar/merchant, journeyed throughout the diaspora, documenting all he saw.

claims.text: לפי אדלר, בתקופת מסעי הצלב הקהילות המשגשגות ביותר בגרמניה והקהילות לאורך הדרך לארץ ישראל הושמדו או התפזרו.
claims.quote: The most prosperous communities in Germany and the Jewish congregations that lay along the route to Palestine had been exterminated or dispersed

claims.text: לפי JTA, במסע הצלב הראשון בסוף המאה ה-11 הטבחו הפרנקים ביהודי צרפת וגרמניה לפני שהמשיכו לארץ הקודש.
claims.quote: During the First Crusade, which took place at the end of the 11th century, the Franks had massacred Jews in France and Germany before continuing to the Holy Land

claims.text: לפי JTA, בנימין לא מספר מדוע יצא למסע מלכתחילה.
claims.quote: he never tells us why he set out on his journey in the first place

claims.text: לפי אדלר, ייתכן שבנימין יצא למסע כדי לברר היכן אחיו המגורשים יוכלו למצוא מקלט.
claims.quote: It is not unlikely, therefore, that Benjamin may have undertaken his journey with the object of finding out where his expatriated brethren might find an asylum.

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, ייתכן שבנימין קיווה למצוא מקומות מקלט ליהודים בארצות שבהן ביקר.
claims.quote: Perhaps he hoped to find places of asylum for his fellow Jews in the lands he visited.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, מטרת מסעו אינה ידועה, ויש שהציעו שהיה סוחר אבנים טובות.
claims.quote: The object of his journey is unknown, though it has been suggested that he was a gem-merchant

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, תיאורו המדוקדק של הפעילות המסחרית מצביע על כך שהיה כנראה סוחר במקצועו.
claims.quote: His careful description of commercial activities indicates that he was probably a merchant by profession.

claims.text: לפי JTA, בנימין חזר הביתה לאחר שביקר ביותר מ-300 ערים וראה מראות מופלאים רבים.
claims.quote: Finally, he returned home, having visited more than 300 cities and seen many extraordinary sights.

claims.text: לפי JTA, כמאה שנה לפני מרקו פולו היה בנימין מטודלה אשכולר וסוחר יהודי מספרד שנסע ברוב העולם הידוע.
claims.quote: A century before Marco Polo, Benjamin of Tudela was a Jewish scholar and merchant from Spain who traveled throughout most of the known world

claims.quote: compiled, as the preface states, from notes made by the traveler on the spot and brought back by him in 1173 to Castile

claims.quote: The unknown author of the preface probably compiled the account for Benjamin from these notes, retaining the traveler's own words in the first person

claims.text: לפי JTA, בנימין מצא בקפריסין כת כופרת שקיבלה את השבת בבוקר יום שבת.

claims.text: לפי JTA, בנימין מצא שבמקומות מסוימים, כמו קושטא ורודבר שבפרס שבה שלטו החשישים, היו יהודים נרדפים באלימות, אך זה היה היוצא מן הכלל.
claims.quote: he found that Jews were violently oppressed. But this was the exception to the rule.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, תיאורו של בנימין את הדרוזים הוא הראשון בספרות הלא-ערבית.
claims.quote: His account of the Druze is the first in the non-Arabic literature.

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, בנימין היה הראשון מהמערב שתיאר במדויק את כת החשישים בסוריה ובאיראן, הראשון שהצביע על האי קיש כמרכז הסחר העיקרי במזרח התיכון, והראשון שהזכיר את סין בשמה המודרני.
claims.quote: He was the first from the West to describe with accuracy the sect of the Assassins in Syria and Iran, the first to point to the island of Kish

claims.text: לפי Legado Andalusí, בנימין כנראה נסע בין 1165 ל-1173 ומת בסביבות 1175, בלי שהספיק לארגן את תצפיותיו.
claims.quote: he probably travelled between 1165 and 1173 and died towards 1175, without having much time to either write or to organize his numerous observations

claims.text: לפי JTA, ספר המסעות נכתב בעברית עם צורות דקדוק ערביות רבות והוא התיאור המפורט ביותר של חיי היומיום בימי הביניים שהגיע אלינו.
claims.quote: written in Hebrew, but with many Arabic grammatical forms, is the most detailed depiction of everyday life in the Middle Ages that has come down to us

claims.text: לפי ההקדמה העברית, בכל מקום שבדקו את דבריו מצאו אותם מדויקים ועקביים, כי הוא איש נאמן.
claims.quote: wherever we have tested his statements we have found them accurate, true to fact and consistent; for he is a trustworthy man.

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, תיאורו של בנימין הוא ללא ספק הרישום המלא והמדויק ביותר של מצב היהודים ומספרם במאה ה-12.
claims.quote: Without question, Benjamin's account is the fullest and most accurate record of the condition and numbers of the Jews in the twelfth century.

claims.text: לפי אדלר, המהדורה הראשונה נדפסה בקושטא ב-1543 על ידי אליעזר בן גרשון ומהדורת פרארה ב-1556.
claims.quote: the Editio Princeps, printed by Eliezer ben Gershon at Constantinople, 1543, and the Ferrara Edition of 1556

claims.text: לפי אדלר, הכרך הראשון של מהדורת אשר, עם נוסח עברי מנוקד, תרגום אנגלי ותיאור ביבליוגרפי, יצא ב-1840.
claims.quote: The first volume appeared in 1840, and contained a carefully compiled Hebrew text with vowel points, together with an English translation and a bibliographical account.

claims.text: לפי JTA, חוקרי הרנסנס גילו את הספר והוא תורגם לשפות אירופיות רבות.
claims.quote: Discovered by Renaissance scholars and translated into many European languages

claims.text: לפי JTA, בנימין עורר השראה ליצירות ספרות חשובות.
claims.quote: Little wonder that he has inspired everything from major works of literature

claims.text: לפי JTA, חוקרים הטילו ספק בהיבטים רבים בנרטיב, ויש שטענו שנפח את מספרי היהודים והגזים בהישגיהם.
claims.quote: Scholars have questioned many aspects of his narrative, with some charging that he inflated the numbers of Jews and exaggerated their accomplishments.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, לא תמיד ברור אם בנימין מונה יחידים או ראשי משפחות, ובמקרים כמו בגדאד המספרים נראים מוגזמים.
claims.quote: though it is not clear in many instances whether he is speaking of individuals or of householders, and in some cases such as Baghdad, the figures seem to be exaggerated

claims.text: לפי JTA, בנימין לא הבהיר שתיאוריו על סין וטיבט אינם מבוססים על ניסיון אישי, שכן מעולם לא הגיע אליהן.
claims.quote: he did not make clear that his descriptions of China and Tibet were not based on personal experience, since he never reached these countries.

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, רוב החוקרים סבורים שתיאוריו על מקומות שמעבר למפרץ הפרסי מבוססים על מה ששמע מסוחרים ונוסעים בבגדאד.
claims.quote: his accounts of places beyond the Persian Gulf are based on what he heard from merchants and other travelers whom he met in Baghdad

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, לגבי מה שבנימין טוען שראה בעצמו נחשפו מעט מאוד טעויות משמעותיות.
claims.quote: regarding those things he claims to have seen himself few significant errors have been exposed

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, הספר אולי אינו נקי לגמרי מבדיון, אך ניכרים בו פיכחון, בהירות סיפור וסגנון תמציתי.
claims.quote: though perhaps not altogether free from fiction, is preponderatingly marked by sobriety and clearness of narrative and a concise style

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, מסעותיו נמשכו לכל הפחות 5 שנים ולכל היותר 14 שנים.
claims.quote: His journeys lasted therefore a minimum of 5 and a maximum of 14 years.

claims.text: לפי הערת My Jewish Learning, מספר היהודים בבגדאד מוגזם מאוד, וחוקרים מעריכים שהיה קרוב ל-4000.
claims.quote: This population figure is greatly exaggerated. Scholars estimate Jewish population in Baghdad at this time was closer to 4000.

claims.text: לפי מאגר אוניברסיטת גרנדה, כתב יד מתועד כהעתק ממהדורת פרארה 1555.
claims.quote: Yemenite script. Was copied from Ferrara 1555 (One page from the beginning is missing).

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, ההקדמה העברית מתארת את בנימין כרב והוא הפגין בקיאות בספרות רבנית.
claims.quote: The Hebrew preface speaks of Benjamin as a rabbi, and in his observations Benjamin demonstrated a familiarity with the rabbinical literature of his time

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, אין סמכות לתואר רבי שניתן לו אלא קיצור מקובל בלבד שקודם לשמו במקורות העבריים.
claims.quote: but there is no authority for this except that the conventional abbreviation

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, בנימין מטודלה היה נוסע יהודי ורב במאה ה-12, הידוע בתיאורו המפורט של מסעותיו באירופה, במזרח התיכון ובצפון אפריקה.
claims.quote: Benjamin of Tudela was a 12th-century Jewish traveler and rabbi known for his detailed account of his journeys through Europe, the Middle East, and North Africa.
